{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Finite-sum bilevel optimization: component gradients and derivative-vector products\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{BL\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}SPEC\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}finite\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}derivative}

Bilevel optimization

Solve the bilevel problem \AtlasInlineMath{\min_x\Phi(x)}, where \AtlasInlineMath{\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))} and \AtlasInlineMath{y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)} is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} and \AtlasInlineMath{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on \AtlasInlineMath{f}, \AtlasInlineMath{g}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\Phi} are specified separately.

\textbf{Status.} Bounds missing

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Bilevel unique reduced; task family: Bilevel

\textbf{MODEL tags.} convexity: Lower objective strongly convex in its lower variable; initialization: Bounded initial potential; initialization: Initial auxiliary domain; structure: Component regularities; structure: Finite sum

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Derivative vector; operation: Component gradient; operation: Cross derivative vector product; operation: Hessian vector product; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function first derivative; scalar derivative order: Scalar-function second derivative

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; computation: Internal arithmetic uncharged; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Outer point x hat

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Reduced-objective gradient norm

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; aggregation: Second moment of the complete error; mode: Expectation; randomness: Algorithm private seed

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} accounting: Joint coordinates retained; budget: Fixed worst-case budget; measure: N grad f; measure: N grad g; measure: N hvp; measure: N jvp; precision: Bit precision not counted

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Solve the bilevel problem \AtlasInlineMath{\min_x\Phi(x)}, where \AtlasInlineMath{\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))} and \AtlasInlineMath{y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)} is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} and \AtlasInlineMath{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on \AtlasInlineMath{f}, \AtlasInlineMath{g}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\Phi} are specified separately.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The upper objective is \AtlasInlineMath{f=n_f^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_f}f_i}. Its components may be nonconvex.

Assume \AtlasInlineMath{g=(1/n_g)\sum_{j=1}^{n_g}g_j}; per-component strong convexity ensures uniqueness of the lower-level mean solution.

Each \AtlasInlineMath{f_i} is twice differentiable. Function values, full gradients, and full Hessians have the respective global joint Lipschitz budgets \AtlasInlineMath{L^F_0,L^F_1,L^F_2}, uniformly across components.

Every \AtlasInlineMath{g_j} is three times differentiable. The full first, second, and third derivatives have the respective global joint Lipschitz budgets \AtlasInlineMath{L^G_1,L^G_2,L^G_3}. Every \AtlasInlineMath{g_j(x,\cdot)} is \AtlasInlineMath{\mu}-strongly convex, uniformly over components.

The objective \AtlasInlineMath{\Phi} is bounded below. The source initial Lyapunov quantity minus \AtlasInlineMath{\inf\Phi} has public finite upper bound \AtlasInlineMath{V_0}, fixed independently of accuracy and component counts. It includes the upper-level gap, lower-level value gap, and an adjoint quadratic potential.

The initial SRBA adjoint vector \AtlasInlineMath{v_0} lies in the known ball \AtlasInlineMath{\|v_0\|\le L^F_0/\mu}. Subsequent projections apply only to this auxiliary vector; x and y may still be queried throughout their Euclidean spaces. Projection onto this known ball is an arithmetic operation, not a hidden projection oracle.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Public inputs are dimension, target accuracy, the model's budgets, and the initial point. The original functions, their lower-level solutions, and the reduced objective are hidden. Queries are restricted to the stated interfaces; inner optima and undeclared derivatives are not available for free.

The interface returns \AtlasInlineMath{(i,x,y), i\in\{1,\ldots,n_f\}\longmapsto \nabla f_i(x,y)}: exact derivatives or derivative-vector products of a selected component. No fresh population-noise oracle is supplied.

\AtlasInlineMath{(j,x,y), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}\longmapsto \nabla g_j(x,y)}. Return the exact derivative or derivative-vector action of the selected component. No fresh noisy population oracle is provided.

\AtlasInlineMath{(j,x,y,v), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}, v\in R^{d_y}\longmapsto (g_j)_{xy}(x,y)v}. Return the exact derivative or derivative-vector product of the selected component. There is no fresh noisy population oracle.

\AtlasInlineMath{(j,x,y,v), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}, v\in R^{d_y}\longmapsto (g_j)_{yy}(x,y)v} The selected component's derivative or derivative-vector action is exact. No fresh noisy population oracle is provided.

The same component index may be used at consecutive iterates. Every operation is still charged separately.

Equation (11), page 5 of the source bundles \AtlasInlineMath{[\nabla F_i,\nabla G_j,(G_j)_{yy}v,(G_j)_{xy}v]}, where \AtlasInlineMath{F_i,G_j} are the upper- and lower-level components. Here the four operations are charged separately. At most four primitive calls simulate one source call; the other responses are not free with one gradient call.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Output one outer point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}. An inner solution, function value, or computable accuracy certificate is not required. Arbitrary admissible postprocessing and unqueried outputs are allowed.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base error is \AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2}. The tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon} is always expressed on the gradient-norm scale. The mean-square requirement is equivalent to the RMS gradient being at most this tolerance.

In this unconstrained model with a strongly convex lower level, \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_x f(x,y^*)-g_{xy}(x,y^*)g_{yy}(x,y^*)^{-1}\nabla_y f(x,y^*)}, where \AtlasInlineMath{g_{xy}=\mathrm{D}_y\nabla_x g} and \AtlasInlineMath{g_{yy}=\mathrm{D}_y\nabla_y g}, and \AtlasInlineMath{y^*} denotes \AtlasInlineMath{y^*(x)}. The identity defines the hypergradient without granting additional query access.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Retain \AtlasInlineMath{(N_{\nabla f},N_{\nabla g},N_J,N_H)}. The scalar bound uses the sum \AtlasInlineMath{N} of four call counts. The algorithm selects components; a full pass costs \AtlasInlineMath{n_f+n_g} gradient calls, with vector products counted separately.

Initialization oracle calls count toward the total. A finite initialization bound is an instance-class assumption, not free access to an inner solver.

The budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path; every actual response within a batch is counted.

Internal processing of available information is free. Comparisons use the explicitly specified scalarization or resource vector. Different resources without given weights cannot be assembled coordinatewise from separate algorithms.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Algorithms may use private randomness. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript. The output may be unqueried, a random selection of a past point, or an admissible average. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential; each actual response in a parallel batch is charged separately. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage using received data are uncharged. Internal operations, memory, and communication are not tracked by this quantity.

Choose one algorithm from the public parameters, then require \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2\le\varepsilon^2} for every admissible instance and legal oracle law. Expectation includes all algorithmic and feedback randomness, with the instance fixed first.

\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed worst-case total number of calls on every execution

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{x,y}: The upper- and lower-level variables. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb R^{d_x},y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f,g}: The original upper- and lower-level real-valued functions. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{f,g:\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x,x_0,y_0}: Output outer point, public outer initial point, and public lower-level initial point \textbf{Domain:} Each lies in its corresponding variable space.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Phi}: The reduced objective. \textbf{Domain:} Defined in the task specification.

\AtlasInlineMath{y^*}: Mapping to the unique lower-level global minimizer \textbf{Domain:} Constraints specified under TASK.

\AtlasInlineMath{\nabla,\|\cdot\|}: Euclidean gradient and vector norm; matrix and higher-derivative norms are the induced Euclidean operator norms

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E,\Pr,\inf,\sup}: Expectation, probability, infimum, and supremum, with aggregation order and randomness specified by the guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{\mathcal O}}: Asymptotic upper, lower, matching-order, and declared-logarithm upper bounds; fixed parameters are specified in each evidence record

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C}: Positive absolute constants or functions of fixed budgets, with dependencies specified by the corresponding result \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c,C<\infty}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target accuracy. Whether error is squared is determined by the metric and guarantee formulas. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{d_x}: Upper-level dimension \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{d_y}: Lower-level dimension \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mu}: The uniform strong-convexity modulus in the lower-level variable. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mu>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{n_f}: Number of upper-level finite-sum components \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{n_g}: Number of lower-level finite-sum components \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{n_{\mathrm{tot}}}: The sum of upper- and lower-level component counts. \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{n_{\mathrm{tot}}=n_f+n_g}

\AtlasInlineMath{L^F_0}: Joint Lipschitz upper bound for each upper-level component value \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{L^F_1}: A joint Lipschitz bound on each upper-level component’s full gradient. \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{L^F_2}: Joint Lipschitz upper bound for each upper component's complete Hessian. \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{L^G_1}: Joint Lipschitz upper bound for each lower component's complete first derivative. \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{L^G_2}: A joint Lipschitz bound on each lower-level component’s full second derivative. \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{L^G_3}: Joint Lipschitz upper bound for the complete third derivative of each lower-level component \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative.

\AtlasInlineMath{V_0}: Public upper bound on the finite-sum derivative method's initial Lyapunov gap, including objective gap and tracking error. \textbf{Domain:} Finite and nonnegative, fixed as accuracy and component count vary.

\AtlasInlineMath{g_{xy},g_{yy}}: Mixed lower-level Hessian block and lower-variable Hessian block \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{g_{xy}\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times d_y},g_{yy}\in\mathbb R^{d_y\times d_y}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{g_{xy}=\mathrm D_y\nabla_xg,\quad g_{yy}=\mathrm D_y\nabla_yg}

\AtlasInlineMath{v}: The algorithm-selected direction for a derivative-vector query. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{v\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f_i,g_j}: Upper- and lower-level component functions in the finite sums \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{1\le i\le n_f,\ 1\le j\le n_g}.

\AtlasInlineMath{i,j}: Upper- and lower-level component indices queried by the algorithm

\AtlasInlineMath{v_0,v_t}: Public initial adjoint vector and the algorithm's adjoint iterates. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{v_0,v_t\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_{\nabla f}}: Upper-level primitive-gradient responses, full or partial as specified by the interface. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative integer. The resource section specifies the runtime-cost guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_{\nabla g}}: Lower-level primitive-gradient responses, full or partial as specified by the interface. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative integer. The resource section specifies the runtime-cost guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_J}: The number of lower cross-derivative-vector responses. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative integer. The resource section specifies the runtime-cost guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_H}: Number of lower-level Hessian-vector product responses \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative integer. The resource section specifies the runtime-cost guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N,Q}: This is the total call budget under the stated resource projection. If only one symbol is used, the two names are aliases for that same budget. \textbf{Domain:} RESOURCE specifies which operations are summed; no additional unit cost is introduced.

\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - target accuracy cost}
\AtlasMath{\begin{gathered}Q^*(\varepsilon)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_\varepsilon}\sup_{I,\mathcal O,\omega}C_{\mathcal A},\\\mathfrak A_\varepsilon=\{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm spec}:\ \forall(I,\mathcal O),\ \mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi_I(\hat x_{\mathcal A})\|^2\le\varepsilon^2\}.\\C=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}+N_J+N_H.\end{gathered}}
\textbf{Scope.} worst admissible instance and arbitrary finite dimension unless model fixes dimensions

\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize resources subject to accuracy

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - Native squared-gradient regime of SRBA}
\textbf{Region.} The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{n_f,n_g} is a positive integer. Hold regularity and initialization budgets fixed, with squared-gradient tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\eta=\varepsilon^2} sufficiently small.

\textbf{Quantity.} Q1

\textbf{Resource.} Sum the unit costs of actual primitive responses in the oracle specification. Separate requests for the two levels cost two calls.

\textbf{Status.} Lower bound missing

\textbf{Lower bound.} B3

\AtlasMath{0\text{ on }r_1\cap r_{\rm zero};\quad\text{unrecorded on }r_1\setminus r_{\rm zero}}
\textbf{Upper bound.} B1, B2

\AtlasMath{\begin{cases}0,&r_1\cap r_{\rm zero},\\O(N+\sqrt{N}\varepsilon^{-2}),&r_1\setminus r_{\rm zero}.\end{cases}}
\textbf{Gap or comparison.} Exact Q*=0 on r1 intersect r\_\allowbreak{}zero, if nonempty; ratio inapplicable there. On r1 outside r\_\allowbreak{}zero, the unrestricted-algorithm lower rate remains missing. The source linear-span lower theorem is not adopted.

\textbf{Comparison argument.} Zero endpoint follows from the explicit baseline-derived proof. The SRBA branch is conditionally retained with its old guard; this is not fresh recertification.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{B1 - SRBA}
\textbf{Admission.} Included in the bracket

\textbf{Direction.} upper

\textbf{Witness or lower-bound scope.} Randomized witness

\AtlasMath{\mathcal{O}\!\left(n_{\mathrm{tot}}+\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{tot}}}\,\varepsilon^{-2}\right),\qquad n_{\mathrm{tot}}=n_f+n_g}
\textbf{Sources.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/dagreou24a/dagreou24a.pdf}{[1]}

\textbf{Dimension conditions.} Valid in every finite dimension of the declared model. No additional dimension dependence is introduced beyond the formula.

\textbf{Oracle correspondence.} The algorithm chooses component indices. Exact component f/g gradients, \AtlasInlineMath{g_{xy}}-vector products, and \AtlasInlineMath{g_{yy}}-vector products are charged separately. A joint tuple in the source can be simulated with at most four such operations, and all scan costs are included. There is no inner-solve primitive.

\textbf{Guarantee conversion.} The native target is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2}, a root-mean-square tolerance, rather than \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|\le\varepsilon^2}. If the source denotes squared-gradient tolerance by \AtlasInlineMath{\eta}, the exact substitution is \AtlasInlineMath{\eta=\varepsilon^2}.

\textbf{Output rule.} Return one outer point \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x}. Expectation uses the oracle and algorithm randomness stated in the contract.

\textbf{Resource conversion.} Charged resources are \AtlasInlineMath{N_{\nabla f}}, \AtlasInlineMath{N_{\nabla g}}, \AtlasInlineMath{N_J}, and \AtlasInlineMath{N_H}. Use a fixed worst-case cap on each execution, not expected calls. Constants may depend on the six declared component-derivative budgets, \AtlasInlineMath{\mu}, and the uniform initial potential \AtlasInlineMath{V_0}. The symbol \AtlasInlineMath{L,\rho,\Delta} is not a parameter of this specification.

\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{N HVP.}

\AtlasMath{O(n_{\mathrm{tot}}+\sqrt n_{\mathrm{tot}}\varepsilon ^{-2})}
\textbf{N JVP.}

\AtlasMath{O(n_{\mathrm{tot}}+\sqrt n_{\mathrm{tot}}\varepsilon ^{-2})}
\textbf{N grad f.}

\AtlasMath{O(n_{\mathrm{tot}}+\sqrt n_{\mathrm{tot}}\varepsilon ^{-2})}
\textbf{N grad g.}

\AtlasMath{O(n_{\mathrm{tot}}+\sqrt n_{\mathrm{tot}}\varepsilon ^{-2})}
\textbf{N inner solve.} 0

\textbf{Constants.} Hold the stated regularity and initialization budgets fixed. Joint optimality is not claimed for parameters whose dependence is untracked.

\textbf{Derivation.} Rename the source upper-level component count \AtlasInlineMath{m} as \AtlasInlineMath{n_f} and the lower-level count \AtlasInlineMath{n} as \AtlasInlineMath{n_g}, and substitute the squared-gradient tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\eta=\varepsilon^2}. Each sampled direction uses only a constant number of the registered component operations.

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/dagreou24a/dagreou24a.pdf}{[1]} pdf pages: 3; 6; 7; section: 2-3; theorem: Corollary 3.6

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Retain the frozen joint Euclidean norm conventions and native hypergradient identity. A differentiable L\textasciicircum{}F\_\allowbreak{}0-Lipschitz component has gradient norm at most L\textasciicircum{}F\_\allowbreak{}0;\allowbreak{} averaging preserves this bound for f. Differentiating each L\textasciicircum{}G\_\allowbreak{}1-Lipschitz gradient gives ||Hess g\_\allowbreak{}j||<=\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}G\_\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} hence ||Hess g||<=\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}G\_\allowbreak{}1 after averaging. At (x,\allowbreak{}y*(x)),\allowbreak{} write Hess g=\allowbreak{}[[A,\allowbreak{}D],\allowbreak{}[D\textasciicircum{}T,\allowbreak{}C]],\allowbreak{} with C>=\allowbreak{}mu I. Set k=\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}G\_\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}mu>=\allowbreak{}1 for a nonempty admissible class. For every w,\allowbreak{} applying Hess g to (0,\allowbreak{}C\textasciicircum{}-1 w) gives ||D C\textasciicircum{}-1 w||\textasciicircum{}2+||w||\textasciicircum{}2 <=\allowbreak{} (L\textasciicircum{}G\_\allowbreak{}1)\textasciicircum{}2 ||C\textasciicircum{}-1 w||\textasciicircum{}2 <=\allowbreak{} k\textasciicircum{}2 ||w||\textasciicircum{}2. Thus ||D C\textasciicircum{}-1||<=\allowbreak{}sqrt(k\textasciicircum{}2-1),\allowbreak{} and the row operator [I,\allowbreak{}-D C\textasciicircum{}-1] has norm at most k. The native identity grad Phi=\allowbreak{}f\_\allowbreak{}x-D C\textasciicircum{}-1 f\_\allowbreak{}y now yields ||grad Phi(x)||<=\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}F\_\allowbreak{}0 k at every x. Output the public outer initial point x0 without querying any interface. The contract requires neither an inner point nor a computed certificate;\allowbreak{} no initialization oracle responses are needed to return x0. For epsilon>=\allowbreak{}L\textasciicircum{}F\_\allowbreak{}0 k the deterministic squared-gradient error is <=\allowbreak{}epsilon\textasciicircum{}2,\allowbreak{} including equality. All four response counts are zero on every execution. Nonnegative response costs imply Q*>=\allowbreak{}0,\allowbreak{} so Q*=\allowbreak{}0 on this sufficient region. The proof covers L\textasciicircum{}F\_\allowbreak{}0=\allowbreak{}0. It asserts no converse below the threshold and is uniform in sample counts and dimensions;\allowbreak{} it uses no V\_\allowbreak{}0 premise.\par\endgroup
